paras: The police beating of a Black woman at Ninth and Santa Fe Avenue was an assault by two officers, Winget and Fritol, on an unnamed "Colored woman" they had arrested, at that corner in Los Angeles on a Friday evening in late June or early July 1919. When a witness, H. A. Reeves, asked about the beating, the officers arrested him. The California Eagle reported the episode as an instance of habitual police mistreatment and announced that local organizations would bring a case against the officers.

According to the Eagle, the scene was witnessed "on last Friday evening" by Reeves, his family and several friends at the corner of Ninth and Santa Fe Avenue. The two officers, described as "of that district," were seen to "seyerely beat and mistreat" a woman whom they had arrested; no charge against her is given. All who saw it, the paper said, considered the treatment "entirely uncalled for," since the woman was sitting on the curb and made no attempt to escape. When Reeves inquired about "such brutal treatment," the officers immediately arrested him.

The Eagle stated that "reputable people" reported the same officers were in the habit of mistreating residents of the district without cause. It announced that "a number of organizations" would institute a case to bring the officers "before the eyes of the law" and urged readers to take an interest. No report of that case, of any action against the officers, of the outcome of Reeves's arrest, or of the woman's name or condition appears in the coverage.

The only known report is a short, unsigned item on the front page of the Los Angeles California Eagle of 5 July 1919, set without a headline of its own beneath a "Sunday School Convention" heading and after an unrelated paragraph. Written from the witnesses' side, it called the scene "very startling" and the treatment "brutal," and it closed with an appeal to readers to involve themselves "for future well-being of all." Because the issue appeared on a Saturday, its "last Friday evening" may refer either to 4 July or to 27 June 1919.
